system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: professional backend work

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Verdane Care hiring team,
I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience team. I am a First
Class Honours Computing graduate with hands-on experience from a software development
internship, freelance work, and substantial academic projects building accessible web
applications using React and TypeScript, alongside Node.js and PostgreSQL experience from
my final-year project. I am drawn to Verdane Care’s focus on putting patients first and making
healthcare simpler and more human. I am a native English speaker.
During my software development internship at Harbourline Media, I worked on its React news
site, resolving accessibility audit issues across more than 20 components, including keyboard
navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels. I also built a reusable, keyboard- and
screen-reader-friendly image gallery, documented it in Storybook, and wrote unit tests with Jest
and React Testing Library; Git/GitHub is also part of my technical toolkit. In my Tidewatch
project, I developed a React and TypeScript interface and a Node.js/Express API backed by
PostgreSQL. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver, and it achieved a Lighthouse
accessibility score of 100.
I would bring a practical, user-focused approach to building patient-facing features, with a
strong interest in accessibility. My freelance work also includes building a Next.js booking
website for a yoga studio, giving me experience with a wellness-related booking context. My
experience with automated unit testing, Storybook and Git/GitHub, which is part of my
technical toolkit, provides a useful foundation for contributing to a collaborative engineering
team, and I am keen to deepen my experience with production backend services and the privacy
requirements of health data.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
experience and approach could contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team.
Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
